answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a nontransferable bond in a vault before it may earn from shared work. A randomly selected peer group checks each claim against signed task records; if the group proves an identity fabricated or duplicative, the bond is slashed and honest reviewers receive part of it. This makes a Sybil attack costly: the attacker must fund many separate bonds and risks losing them, while a jade or timber reward cannot be multiplied merely by creating more names.
